questions.question: Describe what makes a gear a bevel gear and explain why two meshing bevel gears turn the axis of rotation through an angle.
questions.expected_answer: A bevel gear has its teeth cut on the surface of a cone rather than a cylinder, wider at the outer edge and narrower toward the cone's point. Two bevel gears mesh like two cones rolling on each other point to point, and since the cones' axes pass through that shared point at an angle, the two shafts are set at that angle, almost always 90 degrees. The teeth of the driver push the teeth of the driven gear round at the meshing point, so rotation on a horizontal shaft is delivered to a vertical shaft or vice versa, with no slip and a fixed ratio.

questions.question: Calculate the output for a 12-tooth bevel pinion driving a 36-tooth crown wheel at 1800 revolutions per minute, and for a 32-tooth bevel wheel driving an 8-tooth pinion at 60 revolutions per minute, stating the force change in each case.
questions.expected_answer: Ratio is driven teeth over driver teeth. First case: 36 over 12 is 3 to 1, so the crown wheel turns at 1800 divided by 3, which is 600 revolutions per minute, with about three times the turning force, and the axis is turned through 90 degrees; this is the arrangement of a vehicle's final drive. Second case: 8 over 32 is 1 to 4, so the pinion turns at 60 times 4, which is 240 revolutions per minute, with about a quarter of the turning force; this is the arrangement of a hand drill or eggbeater.

questions.question: Give four applications of bevel gears and describe how a bevel pair is sketched and labelled.
questions.expected_answer: Applications: a hand drill, where a large crank wheel drives a small pinion on the chuck shaft for speed; an eggbeater, where one wheel drives two pinions so the beaters counter-rotate; the differential of a rear-wheel-drive bakkie, where a pinion on the propeller shaft drives a large crown wheel for torque and turns the drive across the vehicle; a windmill pump, where blade rotation is turned to a vertical pump shaft. A sketch shows two cones meeting point to point with teeth as short lines on their sloping faces, the shafts at 90 degrees with arrows for direction, tooth counts on each gear, and the ratio and angle written beside.
